messages:
alice: kicking off a canary for release v2.4.0. plan: start at 5%, probe /health every 30s, ramp to 20% over 10m if all green. @ben can you own metrics/watch?

deploy-bot: Canary started id=canary-1950124680; initial_weight=5%; target_weight=20%; ramp_window=10m; probe=/health; alerts=oncall

ben: acked. I'll open the dashboard and watch 5xx, p50/p95, and backend CPU. setting alert thresholds: 5xx > 0.5% or p95 latency +20% -> paging. :eyes:

carol: quick checklist - drain old pool readiness probes will run for 60s, prefix KV cache warmup expected ~2m for typical flows. if cache miss spike, expect some latency blips.

ben: running a sanity curl loop from edge to new pool, 3 parallel threads. cmd: 
```
for i in 1..100; do curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://api.redwood.internal/health; sleep 2; done
```

deploy-bot: probe results (first 2m): 200 x 1200ms avg from new pool; error_rate=0.0% ; canary state=stable at 5%

eva: noticing slight p95 bump on write-heavy traces in the app logs during the first minute, from 380ms -> 580ms. not alarming yet but tagging traces: trace_id=1a2b3c4d

carol: can we hold ramp at 5% for an extra 5m to let KV warm? recommend hold unless errors increase.

alice: good call. hold at 5% for +5m. rollback condition: any 5xx rate >1% OR sustained p95 > baseline+40% for 3m. otherwise proceed.

ben: adjusted ramp_policy -> hold_current_weight. running load-checks against write path, will post results in 3m. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Canary update id=canary-1950124680; weight=5%; status=hold; next_action=auto-ramp after 5m if no alerts

oncall-bot: paging policy attached: oncall@redwood.com will be notified on threshold breach. current oncall: carol

ben: load-check quick stats (after 3m): 5xx=0.2%; p95=610ms (+35% vs baseline). CPU on pool-new 72% (baseline 65%). small cache warm, no errors. my read is safe to ramp to 15% then stop and re-evaluate.

eva: +1 for staged ramp. but keep fallback ready: we should be able to drop to 0% in <30s. what's the rollback command again?

alice: rollback command is here: 
```
rtrctl route set-weight --route api-v1 --pool pool-newv2 --weight 0 && rtrctl route set-weight --route api-v1 --pool pool-old --weight 100
```
(alice: that is run from infra-ops host w/ MFA, will confirm with deploy-bot if triggered)

carol: also pin config in router for 1h to avoid autosmoothing: 
```
rtrctl config set --route api-v1 --pin-duration 3600
```

deploy-bot: Manual ramp to 15% requested by ben; executing... new weight=15% -> success. canary state=running

ben: smoke after ramp: curl health 50/50 -> 200s, p95 now 640ms. 5xx still <0.5%. looks acceptable. continuing watch for 5m.

eva: I'm seeing a few 502 traces tied to a particular shard (shard-7). ramping back could reduce blast radius. recommend we keep at 15% and run a targeted rollback of affected shard routing if possible.

alice: do not partial rollback yet. increase diagnostics: ben attach logs for shard-7 and run one-off test against shard-7 on pool-new. if error reproduces, we rollback full canary.

ben: running targeted test now: 
```
curl -H "x-shard: shard-7" https://api.redwood.internal/endpoint -v
```
response: 502 connection_reset on 2/10, rest 200. attaching logs to thread.

deploy-bot: Alert condition met: 502_rate=0.8% > configured_alert(0.5%). paging carol (oncall).

carol: got paged, checking. I see spike correlates with GC pause on pool-new instance-4. devops to investigate GC flags.

alice: decision: hold at 15% for up to 10m while we attempt quick mitigation (increase heap, GC tuning). if errors persist or 5xx >1% -> immediate rollback. everyone ack?

ben: ack. will instrument GC flags and re-run shard tests in 4m.

eva: ack. I'll prep rollback playbook and ensure we can flip weights in <30s. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary timeline: started 1950124680; current_weight=15%; hold_deadline=1950125560; rollback_command_ready=true

alice: thx team. i'll post final go/no-go after the hold window. keep messages short in thread so oncall sees parity. :rocket:
